findings.reason: a node implementing s2 would add a dead parameter or invent a caller the plan does not name; the interface sentence should drop the resolve-only flag or name who still uses it.
findings.text: s2's unified function keeps "a flag that only resolves", but the sole resolve-only caller was the drain view at `runs.py:2146`, which the change moves to s7, and s7 says the drain view "reads the recorded stall verdict in place of resolving waits a second time" — so the flag is left with no caller

findings.reason: the done-when's "reclassified on the third sweep" needs a history store the section neither names nor has a writer for within its write paths (`recovery_classification.py` + the test only), so the node cannot produce the measure as written.
findings.text: s6 makes the park dead when "the probe's value has not changed across three supervisor sweeps", but the owner it names, `recovery_classification.classify_pointer`, is pure and stateless (it takes one live observation via `recovery_wait._wait_condition_observation`, `recovery_wait.py:393`) and no cross-sweep probe-value history is stored in the pointer, while the only per-sweep actor, `resumption.sweep`, is declared unchanged

findings.reason: the first done-when arm (a population that "last took 900 s" gets a bound above 900 s) has no recorded input unless the node adds a duration record the section does not name; the plan should name the store it is recorded in.
findings.text: s10 sizes each arm's bound from "that population's last recorded duration", read "from the run's own coordinator or earlier landing logs", but the `Measurement`/`Arm` records carry no elapsed time (`landing_measure.py:95-160`) and an arm log holds only pytest output or, on timeout, `timed out after {bound}s` — the configured bound, not the actual duration — so the named sources record no duration

rubric_items.naming: pass — section titles and test names state the mechanism (`test_a_landing_measure_is_bounded_by_what_it_measures.py`, `test_a_park_that_cannot_change_is_dead.py`); no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach a symbol or filename.

rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s2's former second deliverable (readiness-cache retarget) is gone and its one goal is release-on-landing; s6 is one goal (a dead park is classified); s10's bound-sizing and environmental-refusal retry are two mechanisms for the one subject "a landing-measure timeout is not a permanent refusal", proven by a single gate.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every `plan-section-depends-on` entry resolves to a node that exists; s10 (which writes `queue_landing.py`) is transitively ordered after s3 through s8 (`s10 → s8 → s3`), so their shared `queue_landing.py` write path is serialized; s2's write paths cover `promotion.py`, where `discard()` lives (`promotion.py:1892`), so the discard caller it adds is in scope.
